description: Both crates define impl<E> From<E> for BackendSetError<E>. This means BackendSetError<SetError> cannot impl From<SetError> specially, so any code written as BackendSetError::from(set_error) where E=SetError will wrap it in Other(set_error) not SetError(set_error). A backend implementor who writes .map_err(BackendSetError::from) on a SetError-returning function will get Other(SetError(...)) in the dispatch arm for BackendSetError::Other instead of the SetError arm. This is a silent correctness trap for downstream implementors. The fix is to either not derive From<E> for E=Self::Error, or add a special From<SetError> impl that takes precedence (not possible with current orphan rules), or document the limitation very visibly.
notes: mail-server half fixed; waiting for chat-server
title: BackendSetError From<E> blanket impl makes From<SetError> impossible
